title: Ramayana to Release in Nearly 40 Languages in Biggest Indian Film Rollout Ever
excerpt: Namit Malhotra's two-part epic — starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash — opens in the Diwali week with Sony Pictures on international distribution and advance bookings from October 20.
body:
• Ramayana will be dubbed in nearly 40 languages for its worldwide release — the first time an Indian film has been dubbed on such a scale, with the full language list due in a week or two.
  • The two-part mythological epic releases in the Diwali 2026 week: worldwide November 5, internationally November 6 (Sony Pictures), India on Diwali November 8; advance bookings open on Dussehra, October 20.
  • Cast: Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman; directed by Nitesh Tiwari (Dangal), produced by Namit Malhotra, music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.
  • Sony Pictures handles international distribution after the team's CinemaCon 2026 and San Diego Comic-Con push; Part 2 arrives on Diwali 2027.
  • For US readers: this is a theatrical release — expect listings at major chains in metros with large Indian-American audiences (New York, Bay Area, Dallas, Chicago) once advance bookings open October 20.

MUMBAI — Producer Namit Malhotra and his team are mounting the most ambitious overseas rollout ever attempted for an Indian film: Ramayana, Nitesh Tiwari's two-part mythological epic, will release worldwide in nearly 40 languages when it arrives in cinemas this Diwali, trade sources told Bollywood Hungama.

Less than a month from release, the makers have confirmed the film will open in cinemas worldwide in the week of November 5, 2026, with advance bookings commencing on Dussehra, October 20. Getting Sony Pictures on board for international distribution was, in the words of a trade source, "a huge shot in the arm" for a project already positioned as Indian cinema's biggest global swing.

Context & Background: The Franchise Primer

Ramayana adapts one of humanity's oldest epics — the Sanskrit tale of Prince Rama's exile, his wife Sita's abduction by the demon king Ravana, and the war that restores dharma. While the story has been told on Indian screens for a century, this is the first mounting at this scale: a two-part saga, with Part 1 arriving this Diwali and Part 2 scheduled for Diwali 2027.

The production has been building its global case for months. The team's appearances at CinemaCon 2026 and San Diego Comic-Con were deliberate steps toward positioning the film as an international event picture rather than a domestic blockbuster with subtitles, the source said. A dedicated English-language version is part of the release plan, and the dubbed track count — nearly 40 languages — is a first for Indian cinema. Viewers across the world will be able to experience the film in a language they understand, without having to rely on subtitles.

The Cast, the Crew, and the Stakes

The casting is itself a statement of ambition. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, and KGF star Yash plays Ravana — a pan-Indian trio designed to pull audiences from Mumbai to Hyderabad. Sunny Deol plays Lord Hanuman, Ravie Dubey plays Lakshman, and the ensemble includes Rakul Preet Singh, Kajal Aggarwal, Shobana, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, and Vivek Oberoi.

Behind the camera, the pairing is equally pointed: director Nitesh Tiwari, of Dangal (2016) fame, with music composed jointly by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer — a deliberate signal that this film is scoring itself for a global ear. T-Series has bagged the music rights for both parts for a reported Rs. 75 crore in an advance deal.

Impact & Analysis

The 40-language strategy is the real story here. Historically, Indian films reached non-diaspora audiences through festivals or subtitled arthouse releases; a dubbed, day-and-date theatrical rollout across dozens of languages treats the epic like a Marvel-scale franchise launch. If it works, it rewrites the playbook for how Indian tentpoles travel — not as niche ethnic programming, but as event cinema in local languages.

The staggered dating is worth noting: the film releases internationally on November 6, a Friday (the standard international frame), and in India on Diwali, November 8 — two days later, per producer Namit Malhotra's own confirmation to NDTV. Overseas audiences in effect get the first word.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, this is the most accessible a big-screen Indian epic has ever been: a dubbed theatrical release through Sony Pictures means Ramayana should play far beyond the usual diaspora strongholds, and the English version makes it genuinely shareable with non-Indian friends and family. Practical step: mark October 20 (Dussehra) — when advance bookings open — and check your local multiplex listings that week in New York, New Jersey, the Bay Area, Dallas, and Chicago, where Sony's rollout is expected to be widest. If you want the opening-weekend experience in IMAX or premium large format, book early; this one will sell out.

What's Next

The complete list of dubbed languages will be unveiled in a week or two, and the global trailer rollout continues after its earlier postponement to align with the Sony partnership.External reporting: Bollywood Hungama, Pinkvilla.
